RE: Level I Member Appeal – Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Harper Grant
Member ID: W740585624
Reference Number: POC-BA397EFDB1-13824
Date of Notice: 2026-08-23
Requested Service/CPT Code: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction), CPT 28296

To the Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (correction, hallux valgus, with bunionectomy), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23, reference number POC-BA397EFDB1-13824. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

Preliminary note on the policy basis for this denial: The denial letter does not identify, by title, number, or specific criterion, the medical policy or clinical guideline that was applied to reach this determination. I have been unable to independently identify or obtain the specific published Blue Cross NC medical policy or MCG Care Guideline used to evaluate this request. Accordingly, I am not able to quote or rebut specific policy language in this letter, because none was provided to me and I have not been able to verify it independently. I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Blue Cross NC identify by name and number the exact medical policy and/or MCG Care Guideline criteria applied to this determination and provide me with a full copy of that document, along with the specific criterion or criteria in that document that my clinical records were found not to satisfy. Without this information, I am unable to fully respond to the stated basis for denial, and I request that this gap be cured either informally or as part of the appeal review.

In the meantime, I am submitting the following clinical documentation, which I believe demonstrates that this procedure is medically necessary under any reasonable, generally accepted clinical standard for hallux valgus correction surgery (such as documented symptom duration, failed conservative treatment, radiographic severity, and functional impairment):

1. Symptom duration and chronicity: I have experienced 14 months of progressive foot pain that is unrelieved by rest, indicating a persistent, worsening structural problem rather than a transient or self-limited condition.

2. Failed conservative (non-surgical) treatment:
   - Physical therapy: I completed a supervised course of conservative care, including activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic, over 8 weeks (2026-05-23 through 2026-07-18), totaling 24 visits, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - Medication: I was treated with NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief of pain.
   - Injection therapy: I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-12, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.
   Taken together, these records establish that an adequate, well-documented trial of non-operative management was attempted and failed to provide durable relief.

3. Radiographic severity: Weight-bearing foot radiographs obtained on 2026-06-27 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. These measurements reflect a moderate-to-severe structural deformity, which is a standard objective marker used in the clinical literature to support surgical correction when conservative care has failed.

4. Functional impairment and risk of complication: I am unable to tolerate closed shoes because of the deformity, and there is a documented risk of skin ulceration over the bony prominence. This is not a cosmetic concern; it reflects a functional and safety problem that directly affects my ability to wear protective footwear and ambulate safely.

5. Physical examination findings: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, both of which are objective, reproducible findings consistent with a symptomatic, functionally limiting deformity rather than an asymptomatic or purely cosmetic one.

6. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, and my BMI is 29. I am a non-smoker. None of the typical clinical contraindications to elective foot surgery are present in my case.

7. Surgeon assessment: My treating surgeon, Dr. Reyes (orthopedic surgery), has evaluated me and recommended surgical correction with CPT 28296 based on the above findings. I ask that his operative plan and supporting notes, submitted with the original prior authorization request, be reviewed in full as part of this appeal, along with any additional narrative statement or letter of medical necessity he may wish to submit in support of this appeal. [Additional physician letter of medical necessity to be attached, if available]

Given the documented 14-month symptom duration, an 8-week/24-visit course of failed conservative therapy, 8 months of failed NSAID therapy, a corticosteroid injection with only transient benefit, radiographic findings of 38-degree hallux valgus angle and 17-degree intermetatarsal angle, and clear functional impairment (inability to tolerate closed shoes, ulceration risk, positive provocative testing, and pain-limited range of motion), I respectfully request that Blue Cross NC reverse the denial and approve CPT 28296 as medically necessary.

I am enclosing the following supporting documentation with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-23 to 2026-07-18)
- Records of NSAID trial and corticosteroid injection (2026-06-12)
- Weight-bearing foot radiographs and radiology report dated 2026-06-27
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Surgeon's (Dr. Reyes) clinical notes and operative plan
- [Any additional supporting letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23

Please also send me, as part of the appeal record, the specific medical policy or clinical guideline document (title, number, and effective date) that was applied to deny this request, per the request made above.

This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window specified in the denial notice (by 2027-02-19).

Please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address] if any additional information is needed to process this appeal. I also request written confirmation of receipt of this appeal.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Harper Grant
